subject: Post-call: performance targets & SLA language (latency/throughput/streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@acme.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Hi Alex / Sandeep —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance and SLAs so we have an agreed set of items to take into legal/engineering: 

- Business targets you called out:
  - p95 latency target for API responses (streaming) ≤ 150 ms (goal)
  - sustained throughput ~500 requests/minute during peak windows
  - concurrency: ~50 simultaneous chat sessions with streaming enabled
- Streaming requirement: chunked/streaming responses (server-sent events or chunked HTTP) so the front-end can render tokens as they arrive
- Important follow-ups I promised:
  1) Clarify how latency should be measured (request ingress -> last token delivered vs model compute time only)
  2) Exclusions for maintenance, regional outages, bot retries and upstream network issues
  3) Reporting cadence and telemetry: daily/weekly SLO reports, access to traces on the pilot
  4) Draft SLA language and proposed remedies/service credit tiers

Can you confirm the traffic profile (peak periods, average payload sizes) so we can size a pilot? I will loop in Nikhil (sales engineering) and Naomi (customer success) to draft proposed SLA text and monitoring hooks.

Proposed next steps:
- You: share a sample traffic profile CSV (peak minute, typical token lengths) — ideally by EOD Thursday
- Us: deliver a draft SLA snippet + pilot sizing + suggested monitoring dashboard by Wednesday next week
- Quick follow-up call Thursday if anything looks off

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa —

That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p95 150 ms target is measured from client HTTP request timestamp to final token delivered to client (end-to-end). We will accept an SLA measured at the edge if you provide translation to our client-side metrics.
- Peak 500 req/min is for our primary EU/US regions combined; per-region peak is ~300 req/min.
- Concurrency number (50) is per-app instance; we expect to run multiple instances behind a load balancer.

I attached a small traffic profile that shows peak minute rates, average request size, and token length distribution — hopefully helpful for sizing.

We are aligned on exclusions: planned maintenance windows and major cloud provider incidents are reasonable to exclude; we will want to discuss structured retries and how they factor into latency measurement.

Attachment: traffic_profile_q2.csv

I will loop in Procurement for the formal procurement path — happy to do a pilot first.

Regards,
Alex Green
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
alex.green@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Alex — thanks for the fast reply and for the traffic profile. A couple follow-ups (so legal/engineering have crisp asks):

1) Latency measurement
   - We propose the SLA measure be defined as p95 of end-to-end request latency measured at the Redwood ingress gateway (time request received to time last byte/token streamed). We will include translation guidance for client-side measurement to align both sides.
2) Exclusions we plan to include in the draft SLA:
   - Scheduled maintenance with 48h notice
   - Force majeure/cloud provider incidents that impact multiple tenants
   - Customer misconfiguration or traffic patterns outside agreed profile (we will include a margin)
   - Client-side retries that generate duplicated requests (we will document idempotency guidance)
3) Reporting cadence and telemetry
   - Proposed: daily SLO dashboards, weekly roll-ups, and monthly executive report. For the pilot we can provide daily traces and token-level breakdowns for the sample window.
4) Remedies
   - Typical remedy is a graded service credit based on monthly aggregate SLA miss (we will propose tiers in the draft).

Nikhil / Naomi — can you draft a short SLA clause (3-4 bullets) that we can share with Acme legal + a short engineering appendix that describes how we measure latency and where traces will be exposed? Alex, I'll attach the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign link for the pilot below.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789/ACME-2026-RED-0012
Draft SLA docsend: https://docsend.com/d/abcd-Redwood-Draft-SLA

Thanks — I'll aim to get a draft over by Wednesday next week.

Best,
Marissa

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Marissa / Naomi — drafting a compact SLA snippet below (happy to iterate):

--- SLA SNIPPET (draft) ---
Service Availability & Performance SLOs:
- Measurement: p95 end-to-end request latency measured at Redwood ingress (time request received to final byte/token delivered) over a calendar month.
- Target: p95 ≤ 150 ms for streaming responses under agreed traffic profile.
- Throughput: capacity commitment to sustain 500 requests/min aggregated across regions with per-region bursts to 300 req/min.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), force majeure/cloud provider incidents, customer configuration errors, and traffic outside agreed profile.

Reporting & Remedies:
- Reporting: daily SLO dashboards available to the customer, weekly roll-ups, and a monthly executive report.
- Remedies: service credits applied to affected monthly invoice for SLA misses per tiered schedule (0.5% invoice credit for single miss band, up to 10% for prolonged outages) — final percentages to be agreed by legal.

Engineering Appendix (summary):
- Latency instrumentation: ingress timestamps + final token-delivered event.
- Tracing: request-level traces surfaced for pilot windows; aggregate token-level histograms in dashboard.
- Retry handling: best-effort deduplication when idempotency keys are provided; retries from client-side will be excluded from SLA numerator if flagged in logs.

--- end snippet ---

Naomi — can you add notes about how CS will validate customer-side SDK integration and what monitoring hooks we should enable in the pilot? If that looks good, I'll wrap into a PDF and Marissa can send to Acme legal.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
